title: Inkling: Our Open-Weights Model
author: {Thinking Machines Lab}
review: Model identity and parameter counts; no third-party capability scores adopted.
finding: 975B total and 41B active parameters; this study evaluates the text path only.

title: Inkling Model Card
author: {Thinking Machines Lab}
review: Architecture and license sections inspected.
finding: 66 layers, six routed of 256 plus two shared experts; base model is multimodal. This does not establish multimodal support in Cascadia's exported path.

title: Intel Core Ultra X7 Processor 358H: Specifications
author: {Intel Corporation}
review: CPU, memory, GPU and NPU specification tables inspected.
finding: 16 cores/threads (4P+8E+4LPE), Arc B390 with 12 Xe cores, 50 INT8 NPU TOPS, LPDDR5X up to 9600 MT/s. These are SKU capabilities, not measured fleet frequencies or inference rates.

title: Intel Technology Tour 2025: Panther Lake Recap
author: {Intel Corporation}
review: Architecture presentation located; Xe3 family attribution corroborated by Intel's edge white paper.
finding: Panther Lake combines CPU, Xe3 graphics and NPU; heterogeneous accelerators share a client platform, not independent HBM banks.

title: Industrial and Robotics Innovation with Intel Core Ultra Processors (Series 3)
author: {Intel Corporation}
review: Primary vendor description of Xe3 graphics inspected through indexed document text.
finding: Corroborates Xe3 architecture, CPU/GPU/NPU integration; do not substitute generic platform maxima for the installed machines.

title: Pre-Compiled Pipeline Shards for Distributed LLM Inference on Intel AI PC Fleets
author: Berenbaum, Tate and Venkatachalam, Muthaiah
review: Local LaTeX and reproduction files plus public arXiv v1 HTML inspected. Public and local numerical revisions differ; no old speedup imported.
finding: Pipeline shards, Intel iGPU execution, speculative decoding and microbatching are existing Cascadia work. New paper must establish the large-MoE measurement contribution separately.

title: Cascadia: A Control-Plane-Free Alternative to Hyperconverged AI Infrastructure
author: Parij, Matias and Paudel, Pawan and Berenbaum, Tate and Venkatachalam, Muthaiah
review: Local main.tex, claims/reproduction conventions and author information inspected; no publication status inferred.
finding: Supplies Cascadia system context and evidence-map conventions. Its mesh, receipt and availability claims are not measurements of this fixed eleven-stage fleet.

title: Petals: Collaborative Inference and Fine-tuning of Large Models
author: Borzunov, Alexander and Baranchuk, Dmitry and Dettmers, Tim and Ryabinin, Max and Belkada, Younes and Chumachenko, Artem and Samygin, Pavel and Raffel, Colin
review: Primary abstract and companion citation inspected.
finding: Consumer-device pipeline inference predates this study; pooling insufficient individual memories is not new.

title: PRIMA.CPP: Speeding Up 70B-Scale LLM Inference on Low-Resource Everyday Home Clusters
author: Li, Zonghang and Li, Tao and Feng, Wenjiao and Guizani, Mohsen and Yu, Hongfang
review: v1 full HTML, piped-ring design, assignment model and evaluation inspected; later project publication has a different author list, so this citation is explicitly v1.
finding: Ring execution, CPU/GPU layer placement and OS-sensitive memory behavior are prior art. Cascadia measures a resident, much larger sparse model at multiple concurrency regimes.

title: TPI-LLM: Serving 70B-scale LLMs Efficiently on Low-resource Edge Devices
author: Li, Zonghang and Feng, Wenjiao and Guizani, Mohsen and Yu, Hongfang
review: Primary abstract inspected.
finding: Already distinguishes pipeline's single-user limitations from tensor-parallel communication costs; no claim to invent this tradeoff.

title: exo: Run Frontier AI Locally
author: {exo contributors}
review: Official repository inspected as a contemporary system lead; no benchmark comparison inferred.
finding: Distributed local inference is a populated software category. Hardware, model format and workload would need matched measurements for a speed comparison.

title: EdgeMoE: Empowering Sparse Large Language Models on Mobile Devices
author: Yi, Rongjie and Guo, Liwei and Wei, Shiyun and Zhou, Ao and Wang, Shangguang and Xu, Mengwei
review: Primary metadata and abstract inspected; v1 2023, revised v2 2025.
finding: Sparse-model deployment under edge memory limits is established; the specific resident iGPU fleet remains the empirical distinction.

title: PowerInfer: Fast Large Language Model Serving with a Consumer-grade GPU
author: Song, Yixin and Mi, Zeyu and Xie, Haotong and Chen, Haibo
review: Primary abstract inspected.
finding: CPU/GPU exploitation of sparsity on consumer hardware is prior art, though a discrete GPU/host split differs from shared LPDDR memory.

title: Klotski: Efficient Mixture-of-Expert Inference via Expert-Aware Multi-Batch Pipeline
author: Fang, Zhiyuan and Huang, Yuegui and Hong, Zicong and Lyu, Yufeng and Chen, Wuhui and Yu, Yue and Yu, Fan and Zheng, Zibin
review: Full primary HTML and multi-batch offload framing inspected.
finding: Expert-aware batching and pipeline bubbles are existing problems. Our limited gains from additional rows are measurements of this backend, not an inherent no-reuse law for MoE.

title: MegaScale-Infer: Serving Mixture-of-Experts at Scale with Disaggregated Expert Parallelism
author: Zhu, Ruidong and others
review: Full primary HTML and attention/FFN disaggregation design inspected.
finding: Independent scaling of attention and experts and communication-hiding microbatches predate this work; datacenter interconnect assumptions differ.

title: EC2MoE: Adaptive End-Cloud Pipeline Collaboration Enabling Scalable Mixture-of-Experts Inference
author: Yang, Zheming and Hu, Yunqing and Sun, Sheng and Ji, Wen
review: Primary abstract inspected.
finding: Heterogeneous edge/cloud MoE scheduling and routing are prior art. No first distributed edge MoE claim is supportable.

title: Achieving Cloud-Grade SLOs for Local Mixture-of-Experts Inference through CPU-GPU Hybrid Design
author: Wang, Wenxin and Hou, Yule and Ji, Yu and Qu, Peng and Zhang, Youhui
review: Primary abstract, authors, hardware and submission date inspected.
finding: A contemporary CPU/discrete-GPU MoE system already addresses concurrency and prefill/decode overlap. Neither cheap local MoE nor overlap is a unique contribution here.

title: Inkling-NVFP4 (975B) on Eight DGX Spark Systems
author: {emretoktas_openzeka}
kind: first-person deployment report; not peer reviewed
review: Full post inspected; first posted 2026-08-13. TP=8, 128 GB UMA/node, CX-7, NVFP4 and MTP; workload 128 input/128 output, ten rounds per level.
finding: Earlier deployment of the same 975B model on a small UMA cluster defeats broad first-model/first-UMA-cluster claims. Reported C=1 27.3 tok/s and about 62 aggregate at C=4 cannot be compared directly to our different precision/network/concurrency.

title: Orca: A Distributed Serving System for Transformer-Based Generative Models
author: Yu, Gyeong-In and Jeong, Joo Seong and Kim, Geon-Woo and Kim, Soojeong and Chun, Byung-Gon
review: Primary proceedings abstract inspected.
finding: Iteration-level scheduling and selective batching are prior art; the admission bug is an implementation finding.

title: SARATHI: Efficient LLM Inference by Piggybacking Decodes with Chunked Prefills
author: Agrawal, Amey and Panwar, Ashish and Mohan, Jayashree and Kwatra, Nipun and Gulavani, Bhargav S. and Ramjee, Ramachandran
review: Primary abstract inspected, including pipeline uniformity argument.
finding: Chunked prefill and uniform-work batches already address pipeline imbalance. Eight-row windows are a hardware-specific application, not a new scheduling invention.

title: Taming Throughput-Latency Tradeoff in LLM Inference with Sarathi-Serve
author: Agrawal, Amey and others
review: Primary proceedings page inspected.
finding: Latency/throughput tradeoffs in chunked-prefill serving are established; compare mechanisms rather than unrelated speedups.

title: Fast Inference from Transformers via Speculative Decoding
author: Leviathan, Yaniv and Kalman, Matan and Matias, Yossi
review: Primary arXiv abstract and proceedings PDF inspected.
finding: Exact speculative sampling is prior art. Our temperature-zero verification only supports claims about preserving the chosen serving path's greedy output.

title: EAGLE: Speculative Sampling Requires Rethinking Feature Uncertainty
author: Li, Yuhui and Wei, Fangyun and Zhang, Chao and Zhang, Hongyang
review: Primary abstract inspected.
finding: Feature-based drafting and MoE evaluation are established. A proposed fleet-trained feature head is future work, not a result.

title: Better and Faster Large Language Models via Multi-token Prediction
author: Gloeckle, Fabian and Idrissi, Badr Youbi and Roziere, Baptiste and Lopez-Paz, David and Synnaeve, Gabriel
review: Primary abstract inspected.
finding: Multi-token heads and their inference use predate Inkling; measuring the shipped head is characterization, not inventing MTP.

title: MoESD: Unveil Speculative Decoding's Potential for Accelerating Sparse MoE
author: Huang, Zongle and Zhu, Lei and Zhan, Zongyuan and Hu, Ting and Mao, Weikai and Yu, Xianzhi and Liu, Yongpan and Zhang, Tianyu
review: Full primary HTML, target-efficiency and moderate-batch analysis inspected.
finding: Already shows acceptance alone is insufficient and verification cost depends on active experts and batch size. The general speculation argument is not novel.

title: MoE-Spec: Expert Budgeting for Efficient Speculative Decoding
author: McDanel, Bradley and Li, Steven and Surineni, Sruthikesh and Khaitan, Harshit
review: Primary full HTML and expert-budget motivation inspected.
finding: Additional speculative branches activate experts and increase bandwidth pressure. Its expert dropping changes the comparison to the present full top-six path.

title: SpecMoE: A Fast and Efficient Mixture-of-Experts Inference via Self-Assisted Speculative Decoding
author: Bang, Jehyeon and Cho, Eunyeong and Hwang, Ranggi and Chung, Jinha and Rhu, Minsoo
review: Primary abstract inspected.
finding: Self-assisted speculation for memory-constrained MoE is prior art; our shipped-head study adds a negative deployment qualification result.

title: MoEfication: Transformer Feed-forward Layers are Mixtures of Experts
author: Zhang, Zhengyan and Lin, Yankai and Liu, Zhiyuan and Li, Peng and Sun, Maosong and Zhou, Jie
review: Primary publication page inspected.
finding: Dense feed-forward decomposition into experts is established. Preserve all active slices here and describe only the compiler/backend realization as the implementation distinction.

title: MLPMoE: Zero-Shot Architectural Metamorphosis of Dense LLM MLPs into Static Mixture-of-Experts
author: Novikov, Ivan
review: Primary abstract explicitly describes deterministic tensor slicing and summation; HTML unavailable.
finding: Particularly close prior art to the all-active algebra. Do not claim a novel mathematical transformation or first dense-to-MoE mapping.

title: Eliciting Latent Predictions from Transformers with the Tuned Lens
author: Belrose, Nora and Furman, Zach and Smith, Logan and Halawi, Danny and Ostrovsky, Igor and McKinney, Lev and Biderman, Stella and Steinhardt, Jacob
review: Primary metadata inspected.
finding: Intermediate-state vocabulary probes and affine corrections are prior art. Failed early-boundary probes are specific to this study and training protocol.

title: Linux cdc_ncm sysfs ABI
author: {Linux kernel contributors}
review: v7.0 documentation inspected; timer API predates this study by years.
finding: Aggregation timer tuning is an existing interface. Measured RTT improvement and workload consequences are the empirical result.

title: OpenVINO Intel GPU Runtime Configuration Options
author: {OpenVINO contributors}
review: MoE GEMV threshold and grouped GEMM options inspected. Master is mutable; use local hashed 2026.3.1 evidence for the defect claim.
finding: Decode/prefill dispatch is a backend configuration choice, not a new kernel introduced by this work.

title: Roofline: An Insightful Visual Performance Model for Floating-Point Programs and Multicore Architectures
author: Williams, Samuel and Waterman, Andrew and Patterson, David
review: Primary archive located for bandwidth-model attribution.
finding: Byte/time bounds are established performance analysis, and require measured or explicitly assumed bandwidth.

title: OpenVINO 2026.3.1: Compressed Fused Three-GEMM MoE Primitive
author: {OpenVINO contributors}
kind: official GPU plugin source, pinned release
review: Release-tagged primitive interface inspected alongside the Cascadia exporter and runtime call path.
finding: OpenVINO supplies the compressed fused-MoE primitive. Cascadia contributes model-specific graph construction, routing interface, numerical range handling and the resident distributed runtime.

title: OpenVINO 2026.3.1: Tiled MoE Graph Lowering
author: {OpenVINO contributors}
kind: official graph transformation source, pinned release
review: Release-tagged graph matcher inspected against build_layer in the pinned Inkling exporter.
finding: Tiled MoE graph recognition and lowering are upstream mechanisms. Cascadia constructs a matching graph with external Inkling routing and an expert-major compressed representation.

title: SmoothQuant: Accurate and Efficient Post-Training Quantization for Large Language Models
author: Xiao, Guangxuan and Lin, Ji and Seznec, Mickael and Wu, Hao and Demouth, Julien and Han, Song
review: Primary proceedings abstract and bibliographic metadata inspected; broader equivalent-rescaling precedent, not an assertion of identical routing treatment.
finding: Equivalent transformations for numerical range and quantization have prior art. SmoothQuant migrates activation outliers into weights for W8A8; Cascadia uses per-row routing normalization and per-layer up-projection attenuation with FP32 restoration for fused FP16 MoE execution.
